text: Which climate generally produces grapes with higher acidity?
options: Mediterranean Answer: B) Cool and wet Solution: Cool climates slow grape ripening, retaining higher acidity and lower sugar, which contributes to freshness and crispness in wine.

text: Malolactic fermentation in wine primarily converts:
options: Phenolics to tannins Answer: C) Malic acid to lactic acid Solution: This process softens the sharp malic acid, creating a creamier texture and is common in Chardonnay and many red wines.
explanation: This process softens the sharp malic acid, creating a creamier texture and is common in Chardonnay and many red wines.

text: Which grape is typically associated with Northern Rhône?

text: Which of the following is a fortified wine?
options: Chianti Answer: C) Port Solution: Fortified wines have additional spirit added to increase alcohol and preserve sweetness; Port is a classic example.

text: In sparkling wine production, the “Traditional Method” involves:
options: Carbonation using CO₂ injection Answer: B) Secondary fermentation in bottle Solution: This method produces fine bubbles and autolytic flavors like toast, brioche, and nutty notes.

text: Which grape variety is most associated with Burgundy white wines?
options: Viognier Answer: B) Chardonnay Solution: Burgundy whites are predominantly Chardonnay, showing elegance, minerality, and potential for oak aging.

text: What is the main effect of oak aging on wine?
options: Adds flavors like vanilla and spice
Converts sugars to alcohol Answer: C) Adds flavors like vanilla and spice Solution: Oak barrels contribute flavor compounds such as vanillin and toast and can soften tannins in red wines.

text: Which of the following regions is famous for producing Riesling?

text: A wine labeled “Reserva” in Spain indicates:
options: Minimum 12 months aging in oak + bottle
Only red wines Answer: A) Minimum 12 months aging in oak + bottle Solution: Reserva wines are aged longer, resulting in more complexity than standard wines.

text: What is the main purpose of yeast during fermentation?
options: Remove tannins Answer: A) Convert sugar to alcohol Solution: Yeast metabolizes grape sugars into alcohol and CO₂, producing the primary structure of wine.

text: Which grape is associated with Barolo?
options: Tempranillo Answer: A) Nebbiolo Solution: Barolo, in Piedmont, Italy, is made from Nebbiolo, producing highly tannic wines with cherry and tar aromas.

text: Which wine is made using the fortification process?
options: Chablis Answer: B) Sherry Solution: Sherry is fortified with grape spirit to raise alcohol and preserve the wine; styles range from dry (Fino) to sweet (Pedro Ximénez).

text: Which winemaking process reduces acidity in white wine?
options: Filtration Answer: B) Malolactic fermentation Solution: Converts malic acid to softer lactic acid, producing creamier texture and reducing sharpness.

text: Which factor most influences tannin development in red wine?
options: Fermentation temperature Answer: B) Grape ripeness Solution: Tannins develop as grapes ripen; underripe grapes yield harsher tannins, fully ripe grapes produce smoother tannins.

text: Which region is famous for Shiraz/Syrah in Australia?

text: Which factor affects the color intensity of red wine?

text: Which factor is most important for the development of botrytis in sweet wines?
options: Hot, sunny conditions Answer: B) Damp mornings with dry afternoons Solution: Botrytis cinerea (“noble rot”) develops under humid mornings, then dries in the sun, concentrating sugars for sweet wines like Sauternes.
